There's very little (if any) to gain by playing the Redux version of Metro 2033 unless you never played the original before.
It's basically an "upgrade" to Metro 2033: Last Light's engine but doesn't adjust atmosphere or visuals accordingly. For example, the original was based on particle effects, very fine-tuned lighting and the fact that people looked as greasy as everyone would become on shrooms and vodka. In Last Light they dropped most of the particles/lighting and replaced it with way more grass, props and increased textural complexity. Metro 2033 Redux doesn't do that - you get the simple look of Last Light but without what made it great. Feels more like Half Life 2 at times.
Gameplay and control wise, it seems like they took 70% of Last Light and 30% of the Original despite their rather distinct differences. Oh and the cutscenes seem to have changed a lot, too (imho worsened), along with a severe downgrade of Artyoms voice.
That said, I'm not sure why ANYONE should prefer this version over the original. It's not even cheaper!

I love the constant feeling of hopelessness throughout the game. Mutant creatures have overtaken the surface while humans are forced to live in underground tunnels like rats. The outside is so contaminated with toxic materials and radiation that you have to wear a gasmask (permanently) and periodically change its filter so you don't die asphyxiated.
The survival factor is quite present: ammo is scarce, and you have to scavenge every single corpse you find if you want to stand a chance against the cold, heartless and brutal environment. Metro 2033 also shows the true side of human nature: even after the apocalypse, you've still got bandits, commies and nazis grouping up and trying to kill each other. It's truly the survival of the fittest.
You'll stumble upon some nice game mechanics like the dynamic use of lighting to your advantage. Depending on the situation you'll either use the lamp in your helmet or NVG - lights are destructible as well, so if you're afraid of giant lamps giving away your location, you can shoot them from long-range to make stealthing easier. Weapons are customizable, but said customization has a clear limit, so don't get too carried away.
Weapons are varied but their use is very restricted, which annoys me. Basic weapons like the revolver, SMG, AK and shotgun are usable pretty quickly, but special ones like the pneumatic rifle, the railgun and many more are only usable until you reach a certain point in the game (hint: after you complete more than half of the story).
As you can see, my complaints are mostly about small stuff; the game is VERY enjoyable (if you like tense, spooky atmospheres), and even though it's pretty short, there's some replayability in it, especially if you're an achievement hunter.
Make sure to read the PC Gaming Wiki article for this game to know how to skip the startup sequence and increase the FOV, among other things. You shouldn't have to, but at least you can fix it.

Few games have captured the 40K universe like this does, from the voice acting and music, to the beautiful ship designs and weapons. Positioning is a major part of the strategies, similar to 18th century naval warfare and being caught in a bad location can be tricky to overcome.
The game's 4 factions: Imperials, Chaos, Orks and Eldar are all unique with their own playstyle and capture the tabletop game beautifully. As somebody who sadly didn't have the chance to play that before GW ended production (god knows why) I can't thank these guys engough for this. Most of the devs are long-time 40K fans and truly went out of their way to do the IP justice
I would highly recommend this to any warhammer fan (if they've not played this already) and to anybody who is interested in space combat strategy games.

TL;DR:
This is what is advertised.
You get to play Battle Fleet Gothic.
It is in an RTS mode and not turn mode.
If BFG is your thing then pick it up.
40K Lore and Fluff:
It has some for an empire branching story campaign.
Though ships in all fleets have quite similar upgrades the patch today has had some changes to reflect the various historical rules flavor of the armies available.
Fleets:
Imperial Navy: story mode, skirmish mode, multiplayer mode, custom game mode
Chaos: skirmish mode, multiplayer mode, custom game mode
Orks: skirmish mode, multiplayer mode, custom game mode
Eldar: skirmish mode, multiplayer mode, custom game mode
Space Marines: DLC or early adopter, ?
Tao: DLC or early adopter, ?
Game Play:
You can play it in a micro-management-ish method or you can use the tools in the game to automate play.
AI Controls:
You can set AI on or off.
You can set ship attack profile as head on or broadside.
You can set ship approach on range bands of 3k, 6k, 9k and 12k range.
You can set some or all ship abilities to auto-fire. Sometimes this is a good idea. The AI knows that setting a damage trap on top of a velocity robbing trap is a good thing. It has good strategic thought for offensive abilities. It is not always a good idea to have everything on autofire as sometimes abilites are needed to gain advantage or win some battles or to keep ships that are heavily damaged from retreating from the battle.
Emergency repairs that could save a ship get fired off with little thought on autofire. You could be effectively repainting the hull when your repairs could best be used for serious hull repairs and putting out hull damaging fires.  With the patch today some damage is the damage that results in a temporary critical damage that may be repaired with emergency repair.
When the time comes that more than one ship has the abilities for the stasis bomb/plasma bomb combo that plays out beautifully when your fleet has one of each there is an issue from autofire.
The same conditions that look good to the AI of one ship will look great to all other ships in the vicinity. Every stasis bomb in range will trigger in a beautiful looking daisy chain. Every plasma bomb in the vicinity will trigger in a beautiful daisy chain.
The first plasma bomb that goes off will destroy a fleet's worth of stasis and plasma bombs that have yet to ignite.
Autofire is beautiful for small engagements in the 300 to 400 point range in early campaign or skirmish. A pain in mid to late game even at the 300 to 400 point range when more ships have the potential for bombing skills.
It is not a good idea to put all abilities on autofire.  As nice as it could be to have autofire abilities go off when player defined thresholds or events or conditions occur the triggers for autofire are relatively occult and less useful when you have more ships in an engagement.
You can set targeting priorities that will help your AI decide both how to fight and navigate. This is useful for getting to know the game but more than a little odd because it ignores navigational hazards and minefields in its decision making for navigation.
You can slow the game down to get used to playing the game or to time nasty things to do to your opponents.
Truly knowing the game to me would be knowing what to automate, what to do manually and developing good strategies for setting target priority. Do this and the Gothic sector will be yours soon enough.
Story Mode:
There is a story campaign for Imperial Navy play. You get to be an Admiral in a branching story map campaign.
Excellent marks for this. You were given ideas of how to do this in the table top. You get to do this in the electronic version.
You are given one priority mission per campaign turn. You get a variable number of additional deployments for additional missions in the sector to establish sector control. This number increases as you level your fleet up.
The priority missions are a mix of standard grab bag missions and custom missions depending on where you are in the campaign time line and your effectiveness as a fleet commander.
Other Modes:
There is play for Imperial Navy, Orks, Eldar, and Chaos in skirmish, multiplayer and custom game mode.
I have not played nor will I review multiplayer. Not yet at least.  Same for custom games at the moment.
In skirmish mode you play the basic mission types. You level up and gain experience for your fleet with no campaign or deep logistic consequences.
Ship Customization:
The ship customization is both more detailed and less flexible in some ways than the original game.
Ships have abilities, staff, and upgrades that may be customized as you advance through campaign or skirmish.
You can give your fleet individual character down to the ship level with this system.
I like it.
One of the advantages of the table top was that you could take a ship body and customize its loadout or make a standard pattern ship. From what I have seen so far is that you can only take standard pattern ships and run them through the customization mentioned above. The customization is a good thing. A powerful and well thought out system. I miss being able to take any loadout that I can glue to a keel from the table top game though.
Things They Could Do Better:
Make it not crash due to video errors when I play too long.
Allow ships in your fleet to be in more than one hotkey control group.  I would like to use a key, like 1, to select all ships, and then use other keys, 2 or 3 or 4, to select ships by battle group or class.  Ships in your fleet may only be in one hotkey control group.
I would like ships to have different targeting priorities per control group.  Targeting priorities are fleet-based and there are only four priorities being 1, 2, 3 and 4.
For example if you would like for your escort ships to have a targeting priority of 1 for enemy escorts and 2 for enemy capitol ships you would have to set each enemy escort as target priority 1 and each capitol ship as priority 2 and these targeting priorities would be fleet wide and not per battle group.
Let you make your own ship classes. Honestly there aren't a terrible amount of combinations available for weapon modules. I just want access to ALL of them.
In Skirmish mode, and assuming multiplayer mode, you may "Kustomiz" Ork ships.  This customisation effects your loadout and also the cost to deploy the ship.  Selections are limited I would assume in the sake of game balance and there is no full customization available even though upgrades make the ship more expensive to field.
If points are points and balance is administered through points then why not open up full customization? Because they said so and had a budget and several meetings and came to this conclusion and players like me should be happy I guess that there is any ship customization at all?
Have some sort of map campaign, story or not, for skirmish play.
Have an open ended world wide campaign like GW summer events of years passed.
An industrious person could use this product to run their own map, story or open ended world wide campaign if they wanted to do so.
Make the ability to maintain range band relative to other ship in your fleet. Would allow escort class ships, faster ships, to actually ... escort ... slower ships. Would allow for less management for convoy missions. Would allow for loitering around objectives in breakthrough missions. Would allow for battle groups of dissimmilar ships to move as a cohesive unit instead of at their full engine rating. Would allow for more similar control to the base table top game.
Summary:
I bought it once and I would most likely buy it again.  I sure would like to see some improvements like those listed above.
Still better than the new Battlefront.

My favorite puzzle platformer, Braid is a gem that should be played by any one who truly appreciates videogames. The game is honestly the complete package for me. Gorgeous visuals with a  handpainted aesthetic, a sublime soundtrack that fit the various stages of the game, and a story that unfolds in a truly unique manner. Braid was an instant classic for me, and I really can't recommend it enough.
Gameplay starts out plainly enough, running left to right, jumping on platforms and enemies. The main hook however, lies in protagonist Tim's ability to manipulate time. We start out with a simple rewind ability, which works much like an old vcr, which leads to some fairly interesting puzzle elements. More powerful temporal abilities are granted as the game progresses, which adds a good level of complexity to it. The puzzles can be quite challenging in the later stages, but typically don't feel unfair or insurmountable. I'd say my only real gripe with the game are the somewhat pedestrian boss fights. Fortunately the bosses are an incredibly small part of the game, and don't undermine an otherwise sublime experience.
While the gameplay, visuals, and music are firing on all cylinders, it was the story that etched Braid into the pantheon of my favorite games. While appearing as a run of the mill save the damsel  tale, Braid was anything but. As Tim travels between worlds, we get bits and pieces of his past through text passages in books at the end of each level. Without spoiling anything, the story doesn't unfold in the way you'd expect, subverting standard expectations. Do yourself a favor and make sure you get the complete ending (even if you have to use a walkthrough), as the 'real' ending completely reshapes the meaning of the story.
While maybe not for the more action oriented shooter crowd, Braid still holds up 8 years later. Any one looking for something to stimulate the brain should look no further.

Feel free to correct any mistakes I might say.
The game isn't ruined from DLC, or so I say from a casual playing perspective. I don't see this being a competetive RTS- but regardless, it is fun when I play with my older brothers. The game definitely still needs some work, though I haven't had any gamebreaking problems in my ~30 hours these last two weeks.
The current features of the game (as of 1/29/2015) are. . .
-War Spoils System (RNG [random drop rewards you might get after a match]) which isn't entirely bad, but there's too much useless crap in my opinion. Some of the stuff you get doesn't really help much, at least it doesn't help me. Like I've gotten IR Half-Track build time reduction bulletin a couple of times, but I'll probably never use it. You can get commanders, but I've only ever got one commander in my entire career to rank 50+. I also feel that they need to increase the drop rate, since I'd think that there's too much stuff to get- whereas you might not get anything at all from like a 30+min match.
-The most important thing is to capture territories, and what I love about capture points is that you don't have to click to capture- but instead, fortify a position on-point and capture.
-I feel like the cover system in this game matters a whole lot more than when it did in CoH 1. Cover could mean the difference between your engineers fending off a pioneer squad or having to retreat. Positioning really matters in this game.
-This game seems to capitalize on Tankery a lot. I don't think I could've ever managed against Hard A.I w/o tanks considering resources are sometimes too intensive with infantry abilities and such. I especially say that you should have at least a jackson if you play as one of the default American Commanders. Note; make sure to take advantage of the reverse option so you're tank doesn't get shot up in the back.
-The DLC you can essentially compare to toys, you don't need them to have fun- but they are most certainly fun; at least for me they are. That is to say, it's not like I agree with those kinds of practices.
-The campaign follows the russians, but the story isn't that memorable to me; I had a somewhat hard time getting through it.
-You can play maps from the workshop, it can be fun since some people do remakes of some CoH 1 maps.
All in all, you get the game for $40. I got this game on a sale, so I won't complain about DLC considering most of the DLC is like what, $2-$5; easily affordable if you REALLY want a commander. Point is- at least the game isn't the usual FULL $60 that Triple A titles go for.
Sidenotes;
- I play with my older brothers a lot, and you should play with people you know; I see that most multiplayer games are fun when you play with people you know, instead of randoms; and really that's what gaming should be about- having fun. Communicating over skype or any other service and random banter and whatnot can really lighten up the mood of the match- sometimes causing less frustration.
-What's great about the American tanks.
-You can switch between HE and AP on Shermans
-On every tank you can have the vehicle crew leave the tank and do repairs so you don't have to have rear-echalon troops or anyones' engineers nearby to do some engine work.
-If you're going to buy, or farm for a commander I recommend Rifle Company for the "Easy Eights" and veterenized Riflemen and other rifle goodies.
-Amassing conscripts, and only conscripts, against Hard A.I is fun.

First off I almost didnt even try this game because some of the negative reviews, that would have been a mistake!
I dont doubt there were gamebreaking issues early on, but I want to let you know that while many issues still exist, they have not stopped me from enjoying this game immensely! So if you were scared off by the bad reviews or if you purchased and stopped playing because of the issues, I reccommend you return to to this early access game!
For starters it was said the Official Server were unplayable, they are playable, even decent! I have only played on Official Servers for my entire experience. I will say that higher populated servers will have more lag than low populated ones. But even on high population l only have occaisional issues.
I was interested in this game purely based on concept. Then the looks pulled me in. And finally the price point was too good to pass up (half the price of big name titles). Additionally the idea of early access and getting in on the ground floor was cool too. I had been looking for an MMO that was not the same EQ/WoW with a new skin...and the survival aspect seemed like I would be in for a whole new experience! And I was right! Many games have almost zero consequences for death, but this one makes you feel it! And at the same time balances that with getting back on your feet without making you want to give up. You lose your items upon death, and can run to retrieve them, but your level and skills stay in tact. To me that is a perfect balance!
You unlock skills by gaining experience (levels) and by performing certain actions. You need to maintain Health, Hunger, Thirst, Focus (brain power with constant spell use) and constitution which the Goblins will explain for you by knocking you unconcious and taking your stuffz.
The game is 30.02 complete as of the writing of this review. So one should expect a few bugs and glitches, and realize that developers are still working on some core aspects of the game. So if you wonder why this game has a bulky text box that looks like something out of the 1990s understand that things like that will be worked on as more of the finishing touches (aka punch list items) are wrapped up. I dont have any direct information about this but I have been beta testing MMOs since the early 2000s and have an idea of how this works.
So if you were curious about this game but were afraid to try it is my opinion that the reasons for the mixed status have been cleared up!

This is one of my favorite games, I know that it says that I only have 10 hours, but have 50 more offline! I love it because it is fun and enjoyable, but also really challenging and intense. You are never guaranteed victory, towards the later sectors 1 screw up and you could die or find yourself with very little health.
The game also never gets boring for a couple of reasons:
The main one being that each run will be different. In one run you might have a really easy sector 1 and in another you could die in a couple of jumps.
Another thing is that there are a lot of ships and hidden quests to unlock. And yes, the crystal cruiser is worth the trouble, it is my fave ship.
Once you do unlock a few ships you might feel like some are qeaker than others, and that is not necessarily true, some are just suited to different playstyles.
Just a couple of tips:
1) DONT FORGET TO PAUSE! When I first started playing I didn't know you could do that which made the game 100X more difficult! Just press space whenever you start a fight.
2) Save up for a teleporter, it  helps alot, gets you extra money, and it is essential for the boss fight!
3) Take the longest route to the end of the sector, this way you can get as much loot as possible.
4) Dont be afraid to jump away if you feel like you are going to lose a fight, and always keep somebody in the cockpit.
5) Finally, once you have beaten the game a few times I highly recommend installing the FTL Captain's Edition Mod. It adds a lot more to the game and makes it better!
All in all, get this game if you like challenging, yet fun games, it is worth the 10$ easily. And remember, its a rogue-like, so if you die you start over, from scratch!

So over all the game is fun. There are issues however most due to the fact that the game is unpolished. When you play on a high Pop server you will experience Server Dysc, and they are working on the issue. Allot of the 3 week or older reviews no longer apply to the game. A large portion of those issues have been fixed. I however do not recommend you playing with the minimum recommended Requirements. They just don't cover it well enough in my opinion. When flying the game has issues rendering the map bellow you, and when the event happens you will for now experience server lag due to skeletons flying in the air, they did do a fix for this but only reduced the chances of it happening it did not eliminate it all together. By the end of the play session tonight I will have close too if not 400 hours played. Here is a list of what I experience with my pc on the daily in DnL.
Sever Dsyc-Only Slightly I play on a lower pop official server.
Mount Lag-Generally when on a mount or tame while in combat or gathering I experience either delayed damage or rubber banding. The delayed damage just makes combat slower, however the rubber banding is generally very annoying, but solvable by just getting on and off the mount. I believe this is cause by either the tame or Toons collision box getting stuck on the node that has just been used. I have already reported this.
Melee on Low Population Server is very responsive I have little too no issues with it. On occasion it will miss for server issues but does not effect over all combat, when I played on a high pop server the issue was extreme and to my understanding it still is on higher pop servers. The latest patch that was supposed to go out on the 08/20/2017 was supposed to fix this issue however due to unforeseen bugs it was reverted and they are now working on a much healthier version of the patch.
Tame times are very long in game, however compared to ark its pretty short, and over all tame maintance is much less, typically tames don't eat when they don't move. Keep in mind many larger Houses will trade resources for tames, So don't be afraid to ask in chat if anyone is willing.
PvP Balance is still being worked on, and is not perfect by any means.
Currently the game is a bit grindy when it comes to what you need to make things like spells, and magic items. They have responded to the community on Reddit DnL official saying they are looking at the issue.
When you are farming the first 2 stages of growth can be cumbersome when crafting your own fertilizer, however this can be solved by donating gold to vendors in town and buying large bags after you have maxed your skill line out. This also applies to the taming skill tree as well.
The Summoning Circle is bugged, they are aware and are working on the issue, the current work around is to kill the tame that is bugged after saving the tame again.
Currently some parts of the map have holes in them, causing the player too fall through the map, they are aware, but need players to screen shot coordinates by hiting the Del button with a screen shot and submitting it too the Bug Report Email.
Collision in this game is the worst I have ever experienced. I have played many Betas, and 2 other early access games. This will cause you or your tames to get stuck inside each other, they are working on this and have a possible fix in the next patch as of this review.

I am not really a fan of fighting games. Only ones I played before this was Soul Calibur IV for PS3 and Killer Instinct for Super Nintendo. Actually loved both those games... But that being said I had a lot of fun with this game too. I read all the reviews before playing this and I knew online play was limited and I also knew the console version is somewhat superior. Softer looking skin and online play don't matter to me. I just want to play the damn game. No nonesense. And I got what I wanted. So if online play doesn't matter to you either, then please try this game!
The basic mechanics of a fighting game are all there. You get solo play, you get survival arenas where you fight enemy after enemy, time trials and team arenas.
The thing I liked is some of the stages are dynamic. You can be fighting in a quiet old looking apartment, blowing through walls and smashing tables and then bust through another wall onto the yard outside. Or throw your opponent off a tower and jump down to the street below. The changing settings is fast paced and doesn't break the flow of the fight at all. I also appreciate the amount of detail the settings have and the amount of it that can be destroyed. Destroying the environment doesn't appear to alter the stages that much, other than asthetically. Fires bursting from the walls or sparks flying, lots of flashy effects and busted pieces of metal and other things. The amount of environment damage gets pretty intense in prolonged fights.
You only get to choose 4 characters which is a disappointment but it is a free game afterall. The amount of content in the F2P version is incredible. Lots of people complaining about lack of content but I found there was a lot of content especially for a free game. You get all game modes except story mode, you get to choose all stages. All beautifully crafted and high detailed stages, I might add.
I'm not sure if other Dead or Alive games were like this but I had to snicker about the age difference in genders. Female characters appear to range from 12 to 18 years old. Meanwhile male characters look 30-60. I think there's maybe 2 female characters that could be around 25 at the oldest. I'm talking about appearances only though. The actual ages of the characters, as designed by the devs could be different. I'm not sure. I was also surprised to see quite a few free outfits for the characters you can choose. The skimpy outfits for the girls are rediculous but amusing.
I really liked the music in this game. I don't know what it is. I usually turn game music off and play my own music but... I didn't turn the music off for this game so I guess that speaks for itself. Also the sound design of everything else is great too like sound effects etc.
All in all, this is only after maybe 5 hours straight of playtime. The other hours played were afk. But I rather enjoyed this game. There is a crazy amount of DLC with a super price tag but I think you can largely just ignore it and purchase just the main game which you can find here:
It's only CDN$ 43.99 which is CDN$ 1,067.48 cheaper than adding all DLC to cart (CDN$ 1,111.47).
Pros:
All game modes unlocked.
All stages unlocked.
Fully destructible environments.
Dynamic stages.
Excellently designed characters.
Clear and vibrant sound design.
Good music.
Decent options for desired game length and difficulty.
Fun and challenging fighting gameplay.
Fast reacting controls. No clunkiness, at least none that I could find.
Gamepad support. (I'm not sure why it says partial controller support, my gamepad works for everything. never needed mouse or keyboard once in the couple hours of gameplay)
Cute outfits.
Cons:
Way too much DLC comprising mostly of costumes. Costumes only you or people who've purchased the same DLC can see.
Character selection is lacking key features. (no ability to view your character from a different angle)
Character details don't seem to do anything? Had me confused for 10 minutes switching between A-D and seeing no changes. Edit: Changes the colour of the panties.
Neutral:
Story mode requires a DLC purchase (CDN$ 16.99).
Limited online features.
Missing graphical details from the console version.
The really bouncy breasts in this game made me laugh.
Overall, great content and excellent value for a free-to-play game. I recommend it. 10/10

Oh man, this is a blast to play!  It's twin-stick shooter old-school arcade heaven! If you're old enough to remember Robotron 2084 then you'll be right at home here, and if you're familiar with the gameplay of stuff like Geometry Wars, Waves, etc., then you'll enjoy this too.
The mechanics are dirt simple, -you move around the arena and you shoot everything. Dead enemies leave "money" which can be spent on upgrades and weaponry to boost your performance. Money doesn't come quickly though so it takes a long time to fully upgrade things and you'll never get all the power ups possible.  Boss battles come into play but the main thrust is you are constantly mobbed from all sides and have to dodge your way through fusillades that while tough aren't as bad as "bullet hell" games.
Layered overtop of this is delicious pixel visuals that are snazzied up with great special effects not seen in the old arcades. Play this in a dark room with some pizza and a soda for the arcade experience.  OOoohhh.
Only complaint is the intensity never really escalates to a frenzied level, so it's quite possible to play for a long time and feel like you're either AWESOME!!!! or bored and ready to kamikaze yourself and do something else.  Personally I had a great time.

A simple game with simple mechanics which is engrossing and enjoyable to play thanks to its sleek execution, and although a single playthrough is quite short, there is replay value. Having said that, it can be quite jarring seeing the characters say the same things despite choosing different options during each playthrough.
This is only a minor gripe I have with it, though, as overall it's a smartly designed game which affords the player a novel perspective through which to experience the gameplay - from my own experience, it's quite rare to play the part of the culprit in a murder mystery, as most tend to be based on famous fictional detectives and call for the player to take on the role of the sleuth. This makes for an interesting twist on a common genre.
Recommended.

(Revised 06/09/2016)
TL;DR:
This is what is advertised.
You get to play Battle Fleet Gothic.
It is in an RTS mode and not turn mode.
If BFG is your thing then pick it up.
40K Lore and Fluff:
It has some for an empire branching story campaign.
Though ships in all fleets have quite similar upgrades the patch today has had some changes to reflect the various historical rules flavor of the armies available.
Fleets:
Imperial Navy: story mode, skirmish mode, multiplayer mode, custom game mode
Chaos: skirmish mode, multiplayer mode, custom game mode
Orks: skirmish mode, multiplayer mode, custom game mode
Eldar: skirmish mode, multiplayer mode, custom game mode
Space Marines: DLC or early adopter, ?
Tao: DLC or early adopter, ?
Game Play:
You can play it in a micro-management-ish method or you can use the tools in the game to automate play.
AI Controls:
You can set AI on or off.
You can set ship attack profile as head on or broadside.
You can set ship approach on range bands of 3k, 6k, 9k and 12k range.
You can set some or all ship abilities to auto-fire. Sometimes this is a good idea. The AI knows that setting a damage trap on top of a velocity robbing trap is a good thing. It has good strategic thought for offensive abilities. It is not always a good idea to have everything on autofire as sometimes abilites are needed to gain advantage or win some battles or to keep ships that are heavily damaged from retreating from the battle.
Emergency repairs that could save a ship get fired off with little thought on autofire. You could be effectively repainting the hull when your repairs could best be used for serious hull repairs and putting out hull damaging fires.  With the patch today some damage is the damage that results in a temporary critical damage that may be repaired with emergency repair.
When the time comes that more than one ship has the abilities for the stasis bomb/plasma bomb combo that plays out beautifully when your fleet has one of each there is an issue from autofire.
The same conditions that look good to the AI of one ship will look great to all other ships in the vicinity. Every stasis bomb in range will trigger in a beautiful looking daisy chain. Every plasma bomb in the vicinity will trigger in a beautiful daisy chain.
The first plasma bomb that goes off will destroy a fleet's worth of stasis and plasma bombs that have yet to ignite.
Autofire is beautiful for small engagements in the 300 to 400 point range in early campaign or skirmish. A pain in mid to late game even at the 300 to 400 point range when more ships have the potential for bombing skills.
It is not a good idea to put all abilities on autofire.  As nice as it could be to have autofire abilities go off when player defined thresholds or events or conditions occur the triggers for autofire are relatively occult and less useful when you have more ships in an engagement.
You can set targeting priorities that will help your AI decide both how to fight and navigate. This is useful for getting to know the game but more than a little odd because it ignores navigational hazards and minefields in its decision making for navigation.
You can slow the game down to get used to playing the game or to time nasty things to do to your opponents.
Truly knowing the game to me would be knowing what to automate, what to do manually and developing good strategies for setting target priority. Do this and the Gothic sector will be yours soon enough.
Story Mode:
There is a story campaign for Imperial Navy play. You get to be an Admiral in a branching story map campaign.
Excellent marks for this. You were given ideas of how to do this in the table top. You get to do this in the electronic version.
You are given one priority mission per campaign turn. You get a variable number of additional deployments for additional missions in the sector to establish sector control. This number increases as you level your fleet up.
The priority missions are a mix of standard grab bag missions and custom missions depending on where you are in the campaign time line and your effectiveness as a fleet commander.
Other Modes:
There is play for Imperial Navy, Orks, Eldar, and Chaos in skirmish, multiplayer and custom game mode.
I have not played nor will I review multiplayer. Not yet at least.  Same for custom games at the moment.
In skirmish mode you play the basic mission types. You level up and gain experience for your fleet with no campaign or deep logistic consequences.
Ship Customization:
The ship customization is both more detailed and less flexible in some ways than the original game.
Ships have abilities, staff, and upgrades that may be customized as you advance through campaign or skirmish.
You can give your fleet individual character down to the ship level with this system.
I like it.
One of the advantages of the table top was that you could take a ship body and customize its loadout or make a standard pattern ship. From what I have seen so far is that you can only take standard pattern ships and run them through the customization mentioned above. The customization is a good thing. A powerful and well thought out system. I miss being able to take any loadout that I can glue to a keel from the table top game though.
Things They Could Do Better:
Make it not crash due to video errors when I play too long.
Allow ships in your fleet to be in more than one hotkey control group.  I would like to use a key, like 1, to select all ships, and then use other keys, 2 or 3 or 4, to select ships by battle group or class.  Ships in your fleet may only be in one hotkey control group.
I would like ships to have different targeting priorities per control group.  Targeting priorities are fleet-based and there are only four priorities being 1, 2, 3 and 4.
For example if you would like for your escort ships to have a targeting priority of 1 for enemy escorts and 2 for enemy capitol ships you would have to set each enemy escort as target priority 1 and each capitol ship as priority 2 and these targeting priorities would be fleet wide and not per battle group.
Let you make your own ship classes. Honestly there aren't a terrible amount of combinations available for weapon modules. I just want access to ALL of them.
In Skirmish mode, and assuming multiplayer mode, you may "Kustomiz" Ork ships.  This customisation effects your loadout and also the cost to deploy the ship.  Selections are limited I would assume in the sake of game balance and there is no full customization available even though upgrades make the ship more expensive to field.
If points are points and balance is administered through points then why not open up full customization? Because they said so and had a budget and several meetings and came to this conclusion and players like me should be happy I guess that there is any ship customization at all?
Have some sort of map campaign, story or not, for skirmish play.
Have an open ended world wide campaign like GW summer events of years passed.
An industrious person could use this product to run their own map, story or open ended world wide campaign if they wanted to do so.
Make the ability to maintain range band relative to other ship in your fleet. Would allow escort class ships, faster ships, to actually ... escort ... slower ships. Would allow for less management for convoy missions. Would allow for loitering around objectives in breakthrough missions. Would allow for battle groups of dissimmilar ships to move as a cohesive unit instead of at their full engine rating. Would allow for more similar control to the base table top game.
Summary:
I bought it once and I would most likely buy it again.  I sure would like to see some improvements like those listed above.

This game seems very lazy. Most of the content is from SRTT and it's DLC. The only "new" things added were some digital graphics(which got old real fast), some new models for enemies, and the Wardens. Those are pretty much the only new things this game brings.
Before you say "well this game brought super powers in!" keep in mind they already did that in SRTT with DLC. They did polish it up and made it the main feature, but that's it. It's not new.
They did fix the weapons from SRTT though. In SRTT the guns did practically no damage to enemies and the enemies were bullet sponges.
One of the biggest things that♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off about this game was the Enter the Dominatrix DLC. That was a steaming pile. It was just using base game materials for most of the DLC. Then they announce a giant monster is coming and then cut to a story board fight where Birk kills it. You can say they did that as a joke, but the way I see it is that they were too lazy/cheap to actually make it happen. I'm not sure why they brought Donnie into this. They didn't bring Dex back because they thought it would alienate new players, but they bring in a minor character like Donnie? Dex was a big character in SR1.
The base game blows. The side missions are unbearable as each one is the same. It's either "clear out that area", "assasinate that virus", or "hold off this painfully long wave fight". The side missions were so damn repetitve. It was agonizing. There was little incentive to do them anyways. The most you could get was unlocking a door to teleport to. Big whoop. You can glide there faster than you can find a portal, leave the world, go back in and warp there. The one sie mission that stands out is the super powered arena fight, but that blows. It's not fund having to fight people who have super powers when all they do is jump far away for no reason and telekentically throw things at you with pinpoint accuracy which makes you ragdoll. The side mission rewards were not worth the trouble. I would rather not upgrade my guns than have to do the same side mission I just did 3 times already.
The Warden fights were far too annoying. Every single warden fight could only be ended when you button mashed like crazy. That can tire your fingers out quick if you do it frequently. Wardens deterred me from doing most things because I didn't want to deal with the hassle. They aren't even hard to fight. They are just annoying. Especially early game when you have to fight them with the crappy telekenesis power. They wuld have been much more tolerable if they would die like in the training sims where they just pop.
They took out all of the cribs. Yes, I know they did that because Zin-yak wanted to "break" them, but without safe houses, it was just city. No where else to go. I don't know why Volition keeps taking out interior buildings as they progress in their series. SR2 had so many enterable buildings. SR3 had significanly less. SRIV I think has 2(Kinzies old warehouse and the bar). I like to have buildings I can enter. It gets boring when all you do is kill on the street. There's nothing else to do. I liked being able to enter my crib and just sit around or jump off the roof.
I also hated how all the characters were aware it was a simulation, but still didn't really accept what that meant. The loyalty missions were painfully crappy. They knew those "people" were AI, but still talked to them as if they were the real things. They knew they weren't real, but still acted like they were. King went as far as to give the AI Tanya a "second chance" despite "her" being a program meant to kill them and nothing more. The whole "Tanya" AI was a load too. Why would an AI designed by the people who designed the entire simulation need to wrangle up some AI ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s in a digital world? It made no sense. Another part was how they all thought Kinzie's warehouse was "safe". Not a single place is safe there. Zin-Yak can see and change anything he wants there. Kinzie knew this, but suddenly just ignores it. They were going to talk about their plan there instead of talking about it on the ship(which would have made a lot more sense).
Vehicles are useless. I don't know why so many of the DLC packs included vehcles. The moment you start gliding is the moment you never get in a car again. When you upgrade your running to the max, I'm pretty sure you run faster than any car and you have better handling and mobility. The garage is completely useless except for VTOLs.
All the DLC is laughable. They only include a few missions and useless features. The Christmas DLC was the most enjoyable(seems like they actually put a little effort into it with the whole Santa's workshop since it didn't use basegame materials), but it only added 3 missions that were painfully short. All together the DLC equals $30. Most of the DLC packs are completely useless. They add vehicles(which are useless the second you can glide), weapons skins(most are crap), and a few costumes(I wore none of them).
The most fun I had in the game(aside from the first experience with super powers) were the missions where you had to go to the real world and fight. Not the Mech missions. Those were very boring. I'm talking abut the missions where you were on foot. Unfortunately there are very few times you get to do this and you are stuck with 3 guns(unless you cheat some in).
The whole GAt thing♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off. I hated how they killed him in 3, but they kept pushing that he died. Even Phillipe and Viola stated he was dead and they were right there. You think they would wonder why after they got knocked out that Gat was missing. Him being captured made no sense since in SR3 Phillipe and Viola always bring up how he died. Don't get me worng, I love Gat, but that's just bad how they did it. If you make a decision like that you should stick to it. Not screw with the story and have it make no sense.
The whole "Fun Shaundi" character bothered me. She wasn't real, yet everyone acted as if she was. Shaundi(whom I hated since SRTT) would even talk to it as if it was her past self.
The Ship was boring and useless. There was nothing worth doing on it. The only times I ever went on it was when a mission told me to.
After you beat the game there is nothing to do. It gets real boring running around blowing things up. That's all you can do. The side missions are way too tedious to even consider fun. It was worse than SRTT after you beat it. At least in SRTT you could go to zombie island and kill zombies, mess around in your cribs, or fight gangs.
The thing that♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off the most is that the game is basically SRTT.5. The whole game really should have been a DLC pack. Cut out the ridiculous repetitive side missions and the game is pathetically small(aka DLC sized). Even the map is frustrating. It's just the SRTT map with minor alterations(deleting the cribs, adding those annoying domes, those towers, and a few floating platforms). I hated the SRTT map. It was so boring. It was all industrial city. Nothing else. SR2 at least had variations. There was a clean upper class section, a ghetto, a suburban area, a mountain with trees, small islands off the shore that aren't connected by bridges, a trailer park, and much more. The SRTT map had 2 types of areas. Industrial and regular city.
A minor complaint, but of all things to NOT bring from 3, why did they not bring the zombies back? The zombie cheat would have made the game so much more tolerable. The zombies are the one thing that really pulls me to play SRTT again. If SRIV had zombies, I would play it more often since the weapons are far better than SRTT's weapons.
Don't get me wrong, I will still play the game, but I do not reccomend it. If you do insist on getting it, you should either get it used on a console without DLC(trust me, the DLC is NOT worth it) or get it on sale.

This game is like playing chess with soldiers against enemy aliens and deaths are permanant.
The difficulty comes in the form of whether or not your capable of taking out an enemy based on your hit percentage; Zero to 100%. The action is turn based but if you move a charecter only far enough to trigger thier (overwatch) ability you can potentially gain a free hit based on percentage when an enemy comes within firing range. Each class of soldier has unique abilities that make them stand out in an RPG type of way to help form a strategy to eliminate all aliens or complete missions. Also when one of your soldiers dies, they're gone for good.
The game gives your soldiers a random class through promotion from; Assault which is your best form of up-close offense. Snipers are great at eliminating enemies from far away and are dominant when purched in high places. Heavy is your AOE explosive weapons specialists (Be warned, they can cause friendly fire.) and Supports are just that, they carry med packs, can hold more items, and provide a stat boosting smoke screen. The Enemy Within expansion allows you to play as (Mechs) which are large robots and depending on how you cusomize them have devistating ways to eliminate baddies and strike fear into the minds of the invaders.
When fully promoted your soldiers have great benifits to taking down enemies with ease. Weapons and body armor as well as mech suits can be upgraded. The game also carries a short mini game of taking down enemy spaceships, but you don't have much control of that except updraging your Interceptor or "Independence Day" type ship called the "Firestorm" with accuracy, dodging, and a bonus time upgrade.
Your base is a fallout shelter layout and is upgraded through gaining currency, scientists, and engineers by completing missions. Launching satelites to different countries which fund your efforts takes time but earns you more money. Also the "Epic Voice Guy" is the head of the game's council which funds you and gives you missions time to time.
The gameplay is very fun, with good voice acting, and an interesting story. The graphics are nice for its time. 9/10 would kill aliens again.

Mystery Chronicle: One Way Heroics is a remake of the Japanese indie game, One Way Heroics, including content from its expansion One Way Heroics Plus. The original game and its expansion were well regarded for large class variety, high replay value, and being RELATIVELY "fair" as far as roguelikes go. The graphics and character art of the original were relatively amateurish, but had their own charm. So how does Mystery Chronicle stack up to its legacy?
Generally well, but with some caveats.
If you are completely unfamiliar with One Way Heroics, this is the simplest description I can manage: imagine playing a somewhat difficult, old-school JRPG with a variety of tightly interwoven mechanics. Now imagine that every "turn" is precious, and that idleness is swiftly punished, sometimes fatally. The "Shine Raid", a wall of light that turns all in its path to ash, cannot be escaped. It will follow you, an eternal harbinger of death that simultaneously punishes idleness while rewarding careful attention to the world map and being as efficient and economical in your actions as you can. That is One Way Heroics.

In terms of gameplay, the new trap mechanics completely screw up the entire thing as any run is now subject to the mercy of RNG, and it's more dangerous to carry bombs than ever before. The new menu design is significantly worse, with the original game's fast and elegant menu discarded for a largely new one that is slower, requires more steps to do anything, and conveys less information than before.
Towns, dungeons, and other locations no longer have their tiles represented on the minimap, and so the only way to find them is by dumb luck or an area map scroll. Balance changes also impact the game, such as Golems formerly being quite slow to make up for their high strength and sudden apperances at potential Goddess statue locations, but now are fast enough to keep pace with an agile character on top of being several tiles big, which allows them to catch up to you as soon as you reveal the fog.
Had I played longer, I'm sure I would've only found more things to take issue with.
This game is loaded with performance issues, the most significant being regular stuttering with each movement, an issue the devs claim is due to needing to wait for enemies to act with each of your turns and so don't intend to fix, despite that the original game worked the same way and didn't suffer from constant stutter.
I was a huge fan of the original game and expansion, but with Spike Chunsoft clearly having no intention to fix the many issues of this version (beyond making sure it actually runs), I can't recommend it to anyone. Old fans should stick with the old game. Anyone interested in checking it out should check out the old game instead.
As a final note, I tried dozens of times to post this review, and every time I submitted it nothing would happen. I tried changing it to positive, and it went through instantly, where I could then edit it to be negative. That's one last dodgy interaction with this shoddy game.
Edit: Oh, and I totally forgot to mention that the neat online features of the original are now locked behind Twitter integration, and you can't so much as see the window of other players' progress without signing in through Twitter, and also that the translation is a clear ESL job with awkward wording, mistranslations, and basic grammatical errors.

This is one of my favorite games, I know that it says that I only have 10 hours, but have 50 more offline! I love it because it is fun and enjoyable, but also really challenging and intense. You are never guaranteed victory, towards the later sectors 1 screw up and you could die or find yourself with very little health.
The game also never gets boring for a couple of reasons:
The main one being that each run will be different. In one run you might have a really easy sector 1 and in another you could die in a couple of jumps.
Another thing is that there are a lot of ships and hidden quests to unlock. And yes, the crystal cruiser is worth the trouble, it is my fave ship.
Once you do unlock a few ships you might feel like some are qeaker than others, and that is not necessarily true, some are just suited to different playstyles.
Just a couple of tips:
1) DONT FORGET TO PAUSE! When I first started playing I didn't know you could do that which made the game 100X more difficult! Just press space whenever you start a fight.
2) Save up for a teleporter, it  helps alot, gets you extra money, and it is essential for the boss fight!
3) Take the longest route to the end of the sector, this way you can get as much loot as possible.
4) Dont be afraid to jump away if you feel like you are going to lose a fight, and always keep somebody in the cockpit.
5) Finally, once you have beaten the game a few times I highly recommend installing the FTL Captain's Edition Mod. It adds a lot more to the game and makes it better!
All in all, get this game if you like challenging, yet fun games, it is worth the 10$ easily. And remember, its a rogue-like, so if you die you start over, from scratch!

===
Baby's First Hack 'n Slash
===
===
Kronos is essentially a top-down, 2D hack 'n slash game with RPG elements. You will find yourself impersonating the son of a great alchemist, that recently disappeared while performing a dangerous experiment: with his last ritual, he wanted to save his son from the terrible things the breach created by the experiment unleashed.
You will soon find yourself stranded in what a short time before was the huge castle of the Nightingale dynasty, which you and your father always served with honor, now transformed in a living hell, infested by hundreds of monsters and corrupted soldiers alike, all tainted by the darkness released from the experiment. It will be up to you, and you alone, to find a way to stop the horror and banish the evil back from where it came from.
Narrative wise, the game is pretty simple and straightforward, as you can understand by the totally unoriginal and kind of stereotyped incipit, as for the rest of the game, for what i have seen, there will be very few dialogues, and other than some collectible tomes with some lore written in them, informing about the castle activities and other informations, there will generally be very little on the side of the story. you are there, go and stop the evil guys, not much else to say. This could be either a good or bad thing depending what kind of game you like.
===
You will start your adventure with a short tutorial to teach you the game basics, then you will be "free" to do whatever you want. The first thing i noticed after some time playing was that the game doesn't really allow you to go wherever you want, for example, there are four different areas you need to complete in order to retrieve certain items and progress the story, well the game decides for you what area you are starting from, but then where you go from there is up to you.
Talking about quests, apart from the main one, there are none, all the things you need to do are only aimed to fullfill your main objective, there are no NPCs to talkto to get secondary missions, well there are no NPCs at all as far as i know. Not even vendors!
The combat system, which is obviously important for this type of games, is very basic. You can choose between melee weapons(sword, mace, axe), ranged weapons (bow), and magic spells. The character will obviously level up and be able to collect loot around the world, each level will grant you a point to spend in one of the three very basic and short skill trees, each featuring ten skills.
Melee combat is very simplistic, with an idle standard attack type for all weapons, differing only in range and speed depending what weapon you use, no dodge, no parry, no counter systems, no backstabs, forget all of this, you just bash enemies, and that is not necessarily bad, but might left disappointed players who look for a deeper experience.
Ranged combat with bows is alright, it is what you would expect from it, you can use special arrows to change your shots effects, you can either find or craft them at an alchemy table.
Magic combat is what i found being the worst, with the mana regen rate being very low and spells having to be used in large quantities to defeat all the enemies present. Also, spells can be click-spammed, most of them anyway, and this is never good for balance reasons.
Skill trees are very simplistic too, giving out basic bonuses like X more percentage of health, speed, mana, or at most some additional effects to our hits like the chance of transmitting a negative effects to all surrounding enemies near the one we hit. On this side, Kronos does not impress and stays on basic levels, the minimum. This could be good if you look for a simple experience or are new to action RPGs, but will probably disappoint if you already are in the genre.
One special mention has to be made to whoever made the level design, he really liked traps, because literally every inch of the whole map is clustered with them! You need to be very careful at all times or you will be damaged by all sorts of traps, both hidden or in sight, with no way to disable or destroy them, this is really really bad because you will constantly be harrassed by traps everywhere you go. A bad game design choice for sure.
If you happen to die, the game will load the last save you made and you will continue from there. Saving is possible only in specified locations with magic books in them. Dying also, for some reason, makes all the enemies on the map respawn again, problem is some enemy spawns are where save books are, so what happens if you save with very few hit points, then die, and respawn in a room filled with enemies? This is exactly what happened to me, and it is not good at all. Another bad game design choice.
You also will have the chance of collecting various ingredients from enemies and loot crates, and use them in alchemical tables, found around the map. Here you will be able to crreate special arrows, potions and other useful items for your adventure.
Main problem with the gameplay is the lack of depth, everything is too simplistic, there is no stat leveling, no skill synergy, no definite class-building, no spacializations of any relevance, skills are very basic, it is not recommended to anyone looking for a deeper experience.
===
The game uses a basic 2D engine, featuring hand drawn sprites and effects. The art style is well, very simplistic mostly, people are portraited as elleiptic shapes with a circular head and two circle-shaped hands, the decor and environments are drawn alright but again look very simple, there is no real artistic depth in anything, nothing is ugly either it's just... basic, i don't find a better adjective.
The engine is alright, runs well, does the job, but has problems with collisions and hitboxes, especially on narrow passages and doors, enemy hit detection is uncertain, the absecne of any enemy hitting effect really takes away the "feeling" of hitting something, you simply see the enemy stagger away a little with no visible consequences apart damage numbers popping.
A major technical issue is that enemies probably use a basic AI follow script, therefore you can literally aggro and kite around huge mobs of enemies, only to dispatch them all with a few well placed spalls or special arrows. If you don't die for the traps before.
Talking of balance, i played the highest difficulty and there is more than enough challenge that's for sure, enemies will stomp you if you ar enot very careful in what you do. Absence of passive Hp regen adds to the challenge, but may be crippling since there is a finite number of potions that can be crafted or found, and the enemies respawn on every death, so do the math and you will soon know that if you die too much there won't be enough resources for you to get by and advance in the game. This WILL likely happen.
UI is not so good either, i found it very clunky to have different menus for equipment, character status and skills, instead of a single menu maybe with divided tabs, inventory management is sufficent but could have been done in a better way, you will find yourself scrolling a lot since the view space is limited but the invenory is, presumably, bottomless. Also there are no vendors so why piling all the loot?
===
Kronos is a sub-par, barely sufficend action rpg in all fields. Delivers the basic core experience of ARPGs but has many lackings and most of all a lack of DEPTH. For the price range we talk about, it is suggested if discounted and if you want something very basic, or maybe if you are new to the ARPG genre this may be a nice start, but otherwise i suggest moving on to more complex products.

It’s hard for me to find redeeming points in Kronos’ favor. I usually have no such issues since most video games on Steam that I accept to review (I reject shovelware by principle) aren’t both overpriced and simplistic to the point of making browser-based “games”, noteworthy. This title made me reconsider what types of games I’m still willing to write about and even their future number since I’m starting to feel burned-out. If I were to make a tasteless pun, I’d say Kronos has been a waste of my time. Get it? Kronos, is a disambiguation of Chronos/Chronus, the personification of time in Greco-Roman mythology. No? Okay, the nerd will go sit quietly in a corner.
Seriously, though. The dev team made very few efforts in polishing their first and so far only Steam project. Doesn’t seem like a promising debut at all, guys. For starters, who thought that pricing this thing at 7 dollars/euros was a bright idea? Kronos doesn’t even offer Trading Cards at the time of this writing. Don’t even get me started on the “storyline”, since generic doesn’t manage to covey it by proper term. I’m an RPG fan. I clocked more hours on classic 2D RPGs than some gamers have spent so far just shooting their way from one CS or COD map to another. I can appreciate spartan looks if they are coupled at least by a more than decent story/setting/characters. Kronos features none of these, to the point at which you may not overlook the literal slow pacing (the protagonist never heard of running, in his life) and the fact that the many rooms and arenas just seem recycled one after another. And what kind a twisted joke would that be, the case of a role playing game in which you don’t really get to role play? No classes to choose from and definitely no dialogue or NPCs to interact with.
Weaponry, spell and foe diversity are a welcome sight, but the assets themselves are quite repetitive. Stylistically speaking, Kronos attempted minimalism, but failed. Imagine Prison Architect but with next to no charm, zooming in/out and a tenth of its asset variety. Not a pretty picture? My thoughts exactly. So what might this game have to offer that could still compel you to try it out? Some basic crafting mechanics, an inventory system and It features some puzzle segments that mercifully take your mind off the barebones combat sections. Never too hard or complex, you’ll still learn to respect any break from the same old rinse and repeat pattern of wacking melee weapons or shooting fireballs and arrows in the general direction of the enemy (and missing the target most of the time).
Buying this game only once it’s bundled seems like a sound plan while purchasing it directly from the Steam Store at its current pricing would be a tragedy. Too many alternatives to mention them here. One thing is certain: Steam Greenlight really deserves to disappear and perhaps the floodgates of gaming mediocrity on Steam shall be sealed tight once and for all.

The superb soundtrack, ambience sound, visual design and solid gameplay are its major strengths.
Gameplay-wise it is very similar to counterstrike, with some additional mechanics that increase combat depth such as classes, invisibility and visual enhancement filters such as thermo or movement vision, but it only supports the "capture the ghost" gamemode.
Atmosphere wise it is comparable to the anime "ghost in the shell", as it captures alot of its visual design and japanese setting, while keeping a rather melancholic vibe similarly seen in "lain".
The soundtrack, created by Ed Harrison works very well as stand-alone music, being a masterpiece on its own.
Very impressive as a whole, especially in terms of setting and concept design which are outstanding, i managed to establish a very strong emotional connection to the whole universe being displayed.
I really hope now, that it is downloadable trough steam it will increase its entire community and hopefully allow additional gamemodes and maps.

So you are thinking fo buying medow.  You don't know what to expect.  Well read on and I'll tell you the tale of Meadow and the baby badger!
I bought this game knowing nothing.  Inexperienced in the way of the world I just wandered till I found a pack of animals and joined.  I trailed them really; I was always at the back of the pack because my little legs could not keep up with the stronger and older members.  I was amazed at the places that the leaders took up.  I was a child in awe of the strong adults.  We went into a winter wonderland and we found plants and gems.  We stopped and I discovered the pack found a patch of food.  We all ate together and I was able to see the leaders of the pack.  A large black cat, screaming goat, and white bird.
Everyone could see how new I was from the clumsiness of my actions to the shape and pattern of myself.  Everything about me screamed that I would only slow the pack down.  I had nothing to offer.  I knew nothing of the world nor how it functioned.  We started off again and due to my clumsiness I was soon left behind.  I must have taken a wrong turn somewhere.  The controls were not helping my case.
Then I saw the large black cat.  It was walking, not running like the rest of the pack.  Excited to find someone again, I ran to the cat.  The cat spirited a short ways and I followed.  That cat would then slow so I could catch up.  Over and over the cat lead me and soon I was returned to my spot at the bacl at the pack.  But I was not alone.  The cat stayed with me.  Helps me find ways across rivers.  Waited for me while I struggled to even turn around.  At last I was able to grasp how to control my little badger body and the cat moved on to help another.  I will always remember the cat.
The pack found a underground waterfall.  We all frolicked, played, and picked flowers.  On our way out I fell.  I fell so far that I completely lost the pack.  They were moving on.  I cried out, but it was no use.  I tried to find my way out, but I couldn't.  Then a white bird landed in front of me and nearly gave me a heart attack.  However, then I noticed that there was path right by the bird.  I went up the path and soon the bird flew off and I was once again alone.  I cried out but surley they were too far to hear me now.  I was too slow and now I dare not run for fear of falling down again.  But then I heard it.  A soft cry somewhere above me.  I took a few wrong turns but at last I made it to the top again.  There sitting patiently was that ever so kind large black cat.  It waited for me, a clumsy badger cub, to climb all the way back.  That angel of a cat lead me though the rest of the caves, helped me climb rocks, forged a river by my side at my painfully slow pace and reunited me to the pack.  Thank you black cat.  People like you make the game an awesome expericence.
Then after all of this, a large bird convinced the entire pack of almost twenty people to jump off the map.

This game is like playing chess with soldiers against enemy aliens and deaths are permanant.
The difficulty comes in the form of whether or not your capable of taking out an enemy based on your hit percentage; Zero to 100%. The action is turn based but if you move a charecter only far enough to trigger thier (overwatch) ability you can potentially gain a free hit based on percentage when an enemy comes within firing range. Each class of soldier has unique abilities that make them stand out in an RPG type of way to help form a strategy to eliminate all aliens or complete missions. Also when one of your soldiers dies, they're gone for good.
The game gives your soldiers a random class through promotion from; Assault which is your best form of up-close offense. Snipers are great at eliminating enemies from far away and are dominant when purched in high places. Heavy is your AOE explosive weapons specialists (Be warned, they can cause friendly fire.) and Supports are just that, they carry med packs, can hold more items, and provide a stat boosting smoke screen. The Enemy Within expansion allows you to play as (Mechs) which are large robots and depending on how you cusomize them have devistating ways to eliminate baddies and strike fear into the minds of the invaders.
When fully promoted your soldiers have great benifits to taking down enemies with ease. Weapons and body armor as well as mech suits can be upgraded. The game also carries a short mini game of taking down enemy spaceships, but you don't have much control of that except updraging your Interceptor or "Independence Day" type ship called the "Firestorm" with accuracy, dodging, and a bonus time upgrade.
Your base is a fallout shelter layout and is upgraded through gaining currency, scientists, and engineers by completing missions. Launching satelites to different countries which fund your efforts takes time but earns you more money. Also the "Epic Voice Guy" is the head of the game's council which funds you and gives you missions time to time.
The gameplay is very fun, with good voice acting, and an interesting story. The graphics are nice for its time. 9/10 would kill aliens again.

I am a big fan of Might and Delight Studios. After getting Shelter Complete Collection when it first came out, I fell in love with the art style and the idea of playing as an animal in a beautiful environment. The music and lighting really add to the atmosphere as well.
The same can be found in Meadow, except this time in multiplayer. It is simplistic, but in the best way possible. There is no way to type to each other, just squeeks, emotes, and a few actions like jumping and lying down for communication. You can use the features of the game to find others on the map. Majority of gameplay consists of finding others and running as a herd together, jumping for joy when you find someone new, and finding the collectables which unlock aditional emotes, skins, and actions.
Wonderful game and well worth the few dollars. There is no heavy action and you can't die. Just a relaxing exploration, collection game with others and absolutely no possibility of trolls because of the lack of chat system.
I love it and would definatly recommend it to anyone who is looking for a peaceful and artful atmospheric multiplayer. :)
Cheers once again, Might and Delight!

X-COM: Enemy Within is fun to

Your soldiers spot a squad of three aliens, what are your options?

It doesn't matter, the result is always the same. You scratch and claw with everything you have to stay in the fight and then suddenly when it starts getting good, the game is over but you can continue the ridiculously easy challenge as long as you choose to.
Final reasons the game pales compared to the origional:
Seriously, if you liked this game, you must play X-COM: UFO Defense and find out what you are missing.

While Mystery Chronicle doesn't stray far from the formula of the original game and expansion, the updated visuals and new classes offer a little something for those who are a fan of the series. Unfortunately, there are some gameplay concerns that cause this entry to fall just short of being as good as it's predecessor.
▓▒░ PROS ░▒▓
+ Little deviation from what made the original gameplay great.
+ High quality character art.
+ New classes that are enjoyable to play as.
+ Musical/Sound quality roughly on par with the original.
+ Dosey.
▓▒░ CONS ░▒▓
- Twitter integration is required to share and receive adventuring updates.
- Most of the new allies are not nearly as interesting as the allies of the previous entires, and some feel like they only exist as blatant fan service.
- Trap system that is almost as pointless as it is frustrating.
- Menus can be annoying to cycle through mid-game, especially when attempting to pick up items on the ground.
- No conventional way to exit the game.

Overall I find this a very enjoyable game. The tactical combat is challenging, and extremely satisfying when all the pieces fall into place. The custumization of your soldiers is rather good, which only makes it more painful when one of them gets killed. And they WILL get killed, sooner or later.

And enemy sightlines seem absurdly long. Enemy psionics can target you when they can't even see you... etc.
I suppose this slant in the enemy's favor could be a design choice to sell the "this is a desperate struggle" feeling.

Mystery Chronicle is Spike Chunsoft's version/remake of One Way Heroics which is also a part of their Mystery Dungeon series. The thing is, can their higher production value improve on the original game?
Bit of a yes and no there really. Sure, the higher quality art style is great. Nice voice acting too, and heck we even got an Opening now.
But truth be told its actually quite similar to OWH+. There isn't much significant difference other than PVP, Spike Chunsoft-only classes and possibly some balancing changes on their part.
Nonetheless, it is indeed another One Way Heroics game. And I absolutely love it. If you are looking for more of the same. Then go right for it.
There seems to be some technical difficulties though, might be a bit of unoptimized porting in the mix but I'm doing well so far. Just have to get use to the extra clunkiness of the system. You can't... say move through the system as fast as you can in the original One Way Heroics games. Which can be a tad bit annoying, but nothing serious.
Edit: For the record, I find that there are quite alot of people making a tad bit of a fuss over 30FPS. Yes as I mentioned, its slower than the norm. And due to engine differences there can be delays processing enemy and NPC movement which causes stutters in both standard and dash movements. But it in no way impacts the game. This is a Turnbased Roguelike RPG.  Which means RNG, Logic, Planning and Grinding. 30 FPS affects nothing here.

If you have precious few hours to spend on games in your average week, this one will not reward you. Assuming your enjoyment is pegged to your ability to succeed or at least make progress at something like mine is, of course. If you're a clever person, you will have no trouble figuring out exactly what is going wrong and how you would fix it given the resources (crew, upgrades, etc.). Your failure will just happen to come at a time when you don't have those resources, which, as it happens, will be desperately far from the endgame.

One of those games that you can repeatedly play over and over again, and lose a lot of time in.  It's got a lot of depth in terms of its different mechanics: weight, energy, item identification, etc, etc. With a bunch of different heroes that range from your ground fighters to “oh god, avoid anything that may poke me”, you can get a good amount of strategies out of the game as well. It puts decision making at the forefront, and frankly, that's a really good thing. And while the humor and story may not work for everyone, it really worked for me. Good side characters that have interesting and dark elements to them, as you should expect from any Spike Chunsoft game. Now granted, the main story here takes a back seat to those characters, and frankly, could have used a little more development. And performance has been hit and miss for several people. Yes, it's got a 30 FPS lock (and while yes, I understand that people hate that, I think it's less important for a game like this), and while several people have indicated frame drops, I haven't seen anything on two different systems. Granted, the port itself needs some basic work done for it (I mean, there's not a quit menu option on the main screen for gods sake), but to me it's definitely playable. And that's the big draw of this game: replayability, and playing over and over again.
For the price point, it's definitely worth your time.

That's not to say you can't ♥♥♥♥ up, you absolutely can. Choice of Games, if you haven't played one before, are a kind of game/book hybrid focused on branching narrative. A sort of visual novel without the visual part. Their general strenght is that they tend to be strongly thematic and the lack of gameplay means that they can tell more kinds of stories than your typical video game while still keeping the element of interactivity that draws many of us to the medium.
That's choice of games in general but what about this particual choice of game? Heart of the House is a horror story with a focus on investegation in a Victorian setting. It's 360000 words long and took me about 4 hours to complete. There are a whole bunch of choices but as I have only completed the game once at the time of writing I can't say how many of them have a major impact on the story. I did get the feeling that there were quite a few choices of major significance but that's just a guess. What I can say with much more certainty is that this is one of my favorite COGs. It was usually pretty clear what kind of stat was associated with what action and I almost always understood what the choices actually entailed. So it's pretty good on a mechanical level but the true strenght of this game lies in the writing. The atmosphere and tone is just perfect. All the characters are nuanced and sympathetic but no less creepy when they need to be. On a more meta level the story mixes a few sub-genres of horror to make it a little less obvious were the story is going. The genre savy player is still unlikley to be particularly suprised by the ending but it is a welcome measure nontheless.
All in all what we have here is one of the better games of its kind and a fair value proposition. I would personally recomend putting on some suitable music in the background as a good soundtrack is what's missing the most from the otherwise excellent atmosphere.
